newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - FITZPATRICK DENIES KNOWLEDGE OF POISONER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - FITZPATRICK DENIES KNOWLEDGE OF POISONER.

text.p: All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick played down suggestions by former New Zealand coach Laurie Mains that the team had been poisoned by a waitress named Susie just before they lost the 1995 World Cup final in South Africa.
Speaking at a light-hearted news conference on Wednesday to mark the start of a two-match tour of England by the New Zealand Barbarians, Fitzpatrick was cautious in his comments.
" Obviously something did happen," he said. "Laurie obviously feels very strongly about it but I don't think he is making excuses.
"We don't want to take anything away from the South Africans, they are the champions and they beat us in the World Cup final."
Mains claimed in a television interview to launch his autobiography this week that Susie had been paid to poison the All Blacks on the eve of the final, won 15-12 by the Springboks.
He said he had discovered from two sources that the team's tea and coffee had been spiked and he had hired a South African private investigator to find out what had happened.
But Fitzpatrick denied any knowledge of the waitress in question.
"I can't say that I have ever met Susie," he laughed. "We went back to South Africa again this year and we stayed in the same hotel and it may well have been the same chef. We had no problems."
John Hart, the man who succeeded Mains as All Black coach and who is in charge of the Barbarians side, also joined the debate.
"There is no truth in the rumour that our squad of 36 that went to South Africa was made up of 30 players and six chefs," he joked.
